lines.note: Fuvn is fuun, floating cloud, glossed by Vqicumo and a cloud suspended in the air. This is distinct from the preceding bad-fortune homophone.
Fuunna is the adjectival unlucky form, glossed desditoſa and deſafortunada. The doubled n belongs to the adjective boundary, not a nasal abbreviation.
Fuunni supplies the adverb of the preceding unlucky adjective. Aduer. is Portuguese grammatical metalanguage and remains italic.

runs.text: Eſmola que ſe da aos Bõzos por algum

lines.note: Fuxe is fuse, alms to Buddhist monks for a service. Bõzos is embedded in Portuguese; its italic type and nasal abbreviation are preserved.
The payment is for an office or ceremony; Fuxeuo ſu- starts fuse wo suru. The line break divides the verb, not a new entry.
ru completes suru. Dar ſemelhante eſmola means giving that kind of alms, confirming the preceding noun-plus-verb construction.
A separate Fuxe means a patch; Fuxeuo ſuru means patching. Re- continues the Portuguese verb remendar below.
mendar completes the gloss. Cami marks the upper-region variant tçugui wo suru, to patch; the region name visibly shares the italic explanation.

runs.text: Lugar na Catana onde ſe mete a Cõga-

lines.note: Fuxe here is a recess in a sword for the small knife or another implement. The scan reads Lugar and onde, not Lagar/ende; Catana and Cõga- are italic.

runs.text: tana, ou outro inſtrumento de ferro. Vt,

lines.note: tana completes the embedded Cõgatana. The iron implement and the following examples confirm a storage recess, not a winepress despite the OCR's Lagar.
Cogatana buxe and cǒgai buxe name the knife and kogai recesses. The latter has a visible space before buxe; lexical segmentation is kept as printed.
Fuxe, uru, eta is the transitive to lay down. V- begins Vma, horse; the terminal hyphen belongs to that Roman Japanese fragment.
Vma wo fusuru means making a horse fall or lie down. Fusuru is the historical inflected form, not modern fuseru substituted into the text.
The horse gloss ends; Permet. introduces the transferred sense to condemn. It is a semantic extension rather than another Japanese headword.
Fito wo tçumi ni fusuru is to subject a person to punishment. The legal gloss accounts for the superficially physical verb.
The homographic Fuxe means to mend, with X. as a usage label. Qi- begins qirumono; the label is wholly italic in the scan.
rumonouo completes qirumono wo, clothing as object of fusuru. The Japanese and Portuguese both support mending rather than laying down here.

runs.text: Hũa maneira de cubertoura com hũs

lines.note: Fuxego is fusego, a perforated cover associated with a fumigator. Cubertoura is retained as the printed Portuguese form, not modernized.

runs.text: buraquinhos que poẽ ſobre algum perfumador

lines.note: The small holes and perfumador explain the construction of the cover. Poẽ is the visible contracted verb; no silent expansion to poem.
The scent exits through the cover. Polla and ſae are historical forms; the sentence completes the preceding material description.
Fuxegui gives fusegu, resist or defend oneself. The separated-looking de fenderſe is read as defenderſe from visible letters; OCR's long-s reading changed its sense.
Teqi wo fusegu means defending against an enemy. The Portuguese dos ini- continues inimigos below and confirms teqi, not a different q/g reading.
Tentaçam wo fusegu applies the verb to temptation, a Portuguese loan embedded in Japanese. Reſis- begins resistir, not the OCR's Reſu-.
tir completes resistir à tentação. This explicit translation supports the loanword example; its historical spelling is not replaced by modern Portuguese.
Fuxeguiai means resisting each other, with reciprocal ai and historical contracted principal parts. The Portuguese has a word boundary in Reſiſtir de.
Both sides resist, or many fight among themselves. Entreſi is left as printed, without imposing modern spacing.
Fuxeguitatacai combines resistance and fighting. Pelejãdo has its nasal mark over a; the OCR's pelejõdo is inconsistent with both scan and verb.
Fǔxei is wind-sound, paraphrased caje no coye. The long-u mark and coye agree with the explicit wind-noise gloss.
Fǔxei ſuivon pairs wind-sound with water-sound. Enlarged letters read xei rather than xoi; the v in suivon is retained, not normalized to another spelling.
The noise of wind and water finishes that example. Dagoa is the source's joined form, not silently expanded to de agua.
Fuxei here is the miserable floating world, vqiyo. Miſerauel is one Portuguese word; the internal OCR space is spurious.
Fuxen means not expounding further. The scan reads Nobezu. i, followed by Portuguese, not a Japanese Nobezuiai; this matters to the automatic kana.

runs.text: não ſe dilatar mais na carta. S.

lines.note: The letter-writing explanation says not to extend the letter further. S. remains italic and is not part of the Japanese expression.
Fuxeri is lying down, with principal part etta. The final group is worn: enlarged strokes plus the paradigm and NINJAL support etta, not xeua; the uncertain printing is noted rather than concealed.
Defumarſe adds the fumigation sense, consistent with fusego above. The X. label is italic as a whole, not mixed type within one abbreviation.
Fǔxet/fǔjet are variants for circulating uncertain news, fuusetsu/fuu zetsu in modern terms. Final t is historical syllable-final spelling, not an omitted vowel.
Fuxet, tocazu, is not declaring or explaining, distinct from wind-rumour above. Ichi- begins a Buddhist example about a single character.

runs.text: Não declarar nem hũa ſò letra.

lines.note: ji completes ichiji; not even one character is declared. The gloss explicitly supplies letra and confirms ji, while retaining final t in fuxet.
Bup. is a Buddhist usage label, not Japanese body text. Its printed letters are italic; the earlier mixed B/up styling was an OCR artefact.
Fuxi is father and child, chichi/co, i.e. fushi in a Sino-Japanese compound. Go- starts the respectful example rather than another definition.
Go-fuxi no aida ni means between father and child. The translation and following register explanation support the honorific go prefix.
Falando com reſpeito explicitly says the expression is respectful. It qualifies the preceding example rather than altering the kinship definition.
Fuxi, xixezu, is not dying, immortal. Xe is the dictionary's normal se spelling; it is not evidence for an anomalous modern pronunciation.
Fuxifumet is not dying or perishing. The second occurrence is physically split fu-/met; both represent the same component without normalizing the layout.
metno tai completes the immortal substance/body expression. Suſtancia is kept without adding the b expected in modern substância.
Fuxi now means a melodic phrase or tune. Fuxiuo tçu- begins the example about assigning a tune; identical spelling does not imply the previous immortal sense.

runs.text: Dar toada, ou por em canto algũa

lines.note: qiru completes tçuqiru. The enlarged scan reads Dar and algũa, with a small final a rather than a hyphen; the original OCR lost both.
Couſa finishes setting some thing to song. It is a separate physical row of the same Portuguese sentence, not a headword or catchword.
Fuxi is a joint or node, in fingers, bamboo and trees. The scan reads bambùs rather than bambis; the grave-like mark is retained as seen.

runs.text: Hũa certa fruita pera fazer tinta pre-

lines.note: Another Fuxi is a fruit/material used for black dye. The following teeth gloss narrows this to the traditional tooth-blackening material, without rewriting fruita.
ta completes preta: black dye for the teeth. This is explanatory continuation, not a separate occurrence of a Japanese word.
Fuxi, ſu, xita, uita gives the historical forms for lying down. The unusual uita is clearly printed and also present in the headword data; it is not regularized.
Auonoqini fuſu means lying on the back. Vtçu- begins the contrasting prone position, so the two directions should not be conflated.
buqini completes vtçubuqini, prone, supported by de bruços. The spelling is retained rather than modern utsumuki substituted.
Fuxicuſa is an ambush, and fuxicuſa wo suru its verbal expression. The component kusa here belongs to the established military term.

runs.text: Fazer cilada. No Cami ſe diz.

lines.note: The gloss is to lay an ambush; Cami introduces the upper-region alternative machi-. Cami remains visibly italic inside Portuguese.
buxe completes machibuxe, lying in wait. It is not an independent headword despite occupying its own short row.

runs.text: Lugar onde ſe deita algum homem,

lines.note: Fuxido denotes a place for a person to lie down. Fushi-do supplies a transparent compound, while the gloss is broader than a specific bed.
The definition extends the resting place to animals. Keeping this short row avoids losing part of the stated scope.
Fuxifacaxe is melodic phrasing in vocal or instrumental music. The compound is checked against the following tempo explanation, not guessed solely from modern terminology.

runs.text: tos ẽ que ora ſe apreßão, ora tardão com o tõ.

lines.note: The tune alternately hastens and lingers. Apreßão has the compact ligature preserved from OCR; contracted tõ is not expanded to tom.
Fuxigui is glossed vomoi facarazu, not anticipating or comprehending. The scan's f in facarazu and the semantics both contradict tacarazu.
Fuxigui ideqi- starts an unexpected occurrence. Ideqitaru is the historical arise/happen form, not a malformed modern dekita.
taru completes ideqitaru. Aconteceo couſa milagroſa explicitly describes a miraculous occurrence, with historical Portuguese retained.
Não eſperada completes the unexpected quality. This row belongs to the miracle example, not the adjectival entry below.
Fuxiguina and fuxiguino are adjectival variants. Item introduces a further transferred use rather than a new orthographic form.
The dinner example uses fuxiguina self-deprecatingly: an astonishingly poor meal. Yǔmexi is evening food, not a dream despite its visual similarity to yume.
totonoyete xinjǒzu means preparing and offering it respectfully. The Portuguese future Aparelharuos ei confirms the speaker's offer.

runs.text: cea mal feita, & de que vos eſpantareis.

lines.note: The dinner is badly made and will surprise the guest. This deliberately modest host formula is not a literal claim of supernatural food.
Fuxiguini is the adverbial derivative of the preceding adjective. Its short indented row carries morphology without a repeated gloss.
Fuxiguiſa is the abstract degree/noun form. The final ſa belongs to the Japanese derivative, not a Portuguese inflection.
Fuxijen means not thinking of goodness or virtue: fu-shi-zen, 不思善. Ji represents ze in this spelling; the whole is not simply the naturalness adjective shizen.
Fuxijen, fuxiacu pairs not thinking of good and evil. The parallel Portuguese negation makes the Buddhist formula identifiable.
Bup. closes the Buddhist formula. Material after it is faint reversed show-through, not Bupe. bu; the latter OCR additions are removed.
Fuximarobi means falling or rolling down suddenly. Its historical contracted past ǒda is retained and supported by the paradigm.
Fuxime describes a lowered, troubled face. Roſto is face, and ſembrã continues semblante across the next row; no missing hyphen is invented.

runs.text: te como de quẽ fica conuẽcido, & enuergonha-

lines.note: The face belongs to someone refuted or convicted and ashamed. Conuẽcido and quẽ preserve the visible nasal contractions.
Fuximeni naru means taking on that embarrassed expression. The Portuguese says becoming this way, with its continuation below.
The loaded/downcast expression completes the definition. The source's roſto glyph choice is retained rather than inferred from general ligature frequency.
Fuxin is doubt, paraphrased tçumabiracanarazu, not being clear or fully known. This is a different homophone from construction later.
Fuxinni zonzuru or vomô means thinking something doubtful. The long-o form of vomô is retained; both verbs govern the same doubt expression.
Fuxin wo farasu is to dispel doubt, literally clear it away. Faraſu's f is meaningful and fits the Portuguese soltar/botar fora.
Fuxin wo firaqu is another way of resolving doubt. Firaqu corresponds to opening, not a q/g OCR substitution.
Fuxin wo aqiramuru clarifies a doubt. Historical akiramu here means making clear, not automatically modern giving up.
Fuxin wo tô is asking about a doubt. The long-o interrogative verb is consistent with Perguntar and not replaced with another accent on appearance alone.
Fuxin wo sanzuru disperses doubt. Des fa- is retained with its visible space; this is not silently modernized to a joined desfazer.
The Portuguese finishes removing some doubt, then starts fuxin wo caquru. The two examples remain distinct despite their shared object.
caquru means proposing or raising a doubt. It follows directly from the preceding Japanese object, not a fresh entry.
A homographic Fuxin means construction or building works, 普請. It is distinct from the previous doubt sense and its many examples.
Fuxin here means lack of devotion, 不信, with fuxinna fito an undevout person. The cedilla in Indeuação is retained as printed.
mem completes homem indeuoto. This confirms a person's lack of devotion rather than uncertainty about a proposition.
Fuxinna is something of little devotion. The source's deuação spelling is not corrected to modern devoção.
A second adjectival sense is doubtful. This intentionally links two preceding fuxin senses rather than constituting an accidental repeated definition.
Fuxinni is the corresponding adverb. It is a genuine short body row, not running furniture.
Fuxinſa is the abstract noun form; the separate bottom Fuxi is a catchword. Their spatial roles remain distinct.
